maxRulesReached: Rule limit reached ($1 rules max). Delete some rules first
noRulesHint: Add a rule to start proxying cross-origin requests
guideImportDesc: Import an existing config from JSON
targetUrlHint: Leave empty to forward the original URL unchanged — for header/parameter injection only, or to bypass page CORS
invalidRequestHeader: Invalid request header(s), fix them before saving: $1 (names allow letters, digits and !#$%&'*+-.^_`|~; values must not contain line breaks)
invalidResponseHeader: Invalid response header(s), fix them before saving: $1 (names allow letters, digits and !#$%&'*+-.^_`|~; values must not contain line breaks)
exportDesc: Export all proxy rules as a JSON file
exportSanitizeLabel: Share mode: strip credentials from headers and query params
exportSanitizeTip: Strips Authorization, Cookie and similar request/response headers from both the config file and the HAR; the config export additionally drops token-like query-parameter overrides, while the HAR keeps bodies and URLs as captured so the recording still reproduces the problem. The result is safe to share — untick for a complete local backup.
importDesc: Import config from JSON, existing rules will be overwritten
selectFileOrPaste: Select a file or paste JSON config
confirmImport: Importing will overwrite existing rules. Continue?
dnrStatsHint: Rules that only rewrite the URL are redirected by the browser's network layer and produce no per-request logs; this is a rule-level hit count over a rolling 5-minute window. Use the URL match tester to confirm which channel a given URL takes, and note that refreshing too often can exhaust the query quota — the counts then still come from the previous query
dnrStatsEmpty: No DNR hits in the last 5 minutes
noMatch: Rule does not match this URL
templateDesc: Click a template to quickly create a rule with pre-filled settings
wildcardApiProxyDesc: Redirect all requests from one domain to another using wildcards
prefixPathProxyDesc: Redirect API paths across domains, e.g. v1 → v2
addAuthHeaderDesc: Inject an Authorization: Bearer header into matched requests
customHeaderOverrideDesc: Override specific request headers for matched URLs
undoExpired: Undo window closed — the rule has been deleted
requestBodyOverridePlaceholder: Enter request body to override original (e.g. JSON)
exportHarDesc: Export captured request/response logs as HAR format
exportHarRedacted: Share mode is on: the HAR drops credential headers such as Authorization and Cookie (bodies unchanged).
exportHarFull: Share mode is off: the HAR is written exactly as captured, including real site headers. Do not forward it as-is.
importHarDesc: Import HAR file to auto-create proxy rules from traffic
detailNoData: No detail data captured for this request
detailBodyBinary: Binary response bodies are not stored in the local log — text responses only
mockBodyPlaceholder: Enter mock response body (JSON, text, etc.)
mockIgnored: Mock is enabled but body, status and conditions are all empty — Mock won't be saved
swStatsHint: Hit counts for rules processed by the Service Worker channel (recounted from zero after a config change or when the service worker is recycled)
confirmImportMerge: Merge will add non-duplicate rules from the import. Continue?
wsRuleHint: Also applies to WebSocket: only URL rewrite, query parameters and blocking take effect; header/body/response overrides, mock, delay, retry and sending cookies do not apply to sockets
hitStatsNetNotApplicable: This rule is proxied by the extension channel, not the network layer
hitStatsExtTip: Extension-channel (SW) hits: since the last config change or worker restart
hitStatsExtNotApplicable: This rule redirects at the network layer, not through the extension channel
conflictWarningMsg: This rule has the same match pattern as rule "$1" which has higher priority. This rule may never fire.
dnrSkippedIntro: This rule goes through the DNR channel, but Chrome will not apply it.
dnrSkippedRe2: The regex uses syntax RE2 does not support (lookaround, backreferences).
dnrSkippedSubstitution: The target URL references a capture group that does not exist.
dnrSkippedHint: Switch to wildcard or prefix matching, or give the rule a SW-only capability (method filter, header override, ...) so it runs through the proxy channel instead.
dnrSkippedSummary: $1 of them will not be applied by Chrome
dnrSkippedMsg: Rule saved, but Chrome will not apply it: $1
profilesDesc: Save the current rule set as a named snapshot and switch between environments (e.g. FAT / UAT / PROD) with one click.
profilesNoRulesHint: There are no rules to save
profilesEmptyHint: Save your current rules as a snapshot to switch between environments quickly
confirmLoadProfile: Loading "$1" will REPLACE the current rule set ($2 rules). Continue?
autoOffHint: Automatically turns the proxy off after the set duration while enabled, preventing forgotten proxy sessions
variablesHint: Write tokens and other secrets in your rules as {{NAME}} to reference variables stored here: the real values live in one local place and never leave through an exported config file or a page-side script.
variablesOrphanWarning: Rules reference variables that no longer exist: $1
variableNameInvalid: Names must start with a letter and contain only letters, digits, underscore, dot and hyphen — up to 64 characters
variablesDropped: $1 variable(s) were ignored for an invalid name or length — fix them and try again
variablesLoadFailed: Couldn't load credential variables — the list below is not the current state. Close and reopen this dialog.
variablesWriteBlocked: Credential variables couldn't be read, so this overwrite was blocked (it would wipe the stored ones). Reopen this dialog.
confirmDeleteVariable: $1 rule(s) currently reference it. After deletion those requests send the literal {{NAME}} and will most likely fail. Delete anyway?
undefinedVariableError: The rule references undefined variables: $1. Create them under Settings → Credential Variables, or fix the reference.
variableWsQueryUnsupportedError: Query parameters of a WebSocket rule are built page-side, which cannot read the variable store — {{NAME}} references are not supported there.
headerOverridesHint: Values may reference credentials stored under Settings → Credential Variables as {{NAME}}, so exporting or sharing the config never carries the real value.
createRuleFromLogFailed: Failed to create rule: cannot parse request URL
importCurlDesc: Paste a cURL command (e.g. DevTools "Copy as cURL") to prefill a rule automatically
importCurlSuccess: cURL parsed. Confirm and save in the rule form
importCurlFailed: Failed to parse cURL: no valid request found
urlTestPlaceholder: Enter a URL to preview match results in real time
urlTestHint: Enter a URL to see the matched rule, rewritten URL and forwarding channel in real time
urlTestProxyOff: Proxy is disabled, rules will not take effect
urlTestNoMatchDesc: This URL will not be rewritten and will be sent as-is
urlTestCorsNote: DNR only rewrites the request URL at the network layer — the response never passes through the extension, so Chrome still enforces CORS: if the target environment doesn't return a matching Access-Control-Allow-Origin, the request is blocked. Add any advanced capability (header override, method filter, mock, ...) and the rule switches to extension-side fetching, which is exempt from CORS.
urlTestShadowedTitle: Also matched but shadowed by the rule above:
methodsHint: Proxy only these HTTP methods. Leave empty to match any. Setting methods routes the rule through the Service Worker.
queryOverridesHint: Append or override query parameters on the final proxied URL (Service Worker channel). Values may reference a credential stored under Settings → Credential Variables as {{NAME}} (except on WebSocket rules).
sendCredentialsHint: Sends the target environment's cookies with proxied requests (Service Worker channel) so session-guarded endpoints work. Every request this rule matches then carries your login state there — enable it only for trusted environments.
migrateTargetsDesc: Replace part of the target URL across the selected rules (e.g. switch the target domain when environments rotate).
migrateFindPlaceholder: Text to find in target URL, e.g. uat-api.example.com
migrateNoSelection: Select at least one rule to migrate.
migrateNoMatch: No selected rule target contains the search text.
migrateFindRequired: Enter the text to find to preview changes.
